feed.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion

entry.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
entry.summary:
Recent discussions have shed light on the intricate dynamics of coinbase payouts and decentralized mining pools. Current data demonstrates that it remains possible to discover new blocks, with most Bitmain hardware supporting up to 25 outputs in total. While there is no definitive official source documenting these figures, third-party implementations provide insight into practical limitations, as seen in projects like [DATUM](https://github.com/OCEAN-xyz/datum_gateway/blob/85a19fd48caed0d00e2d26045916d30f84b0668a/src/datum_stratum.cL1675%28%29). For those seeking further conceptual grounding, additional discussion can be found in this [footnote](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/decentralized-coinbase-payout-protocols-dcpp-a-framework-for-discussion/3060footnote-9019-2).
Both rapid honest growth (RLA) and a pool reaching its scaling limits result in similar symptoms for decentralized mining operations. However, honest expansion should not be equated with malicious activity; rather, it represents an inherent constraint of the protocol itself. Among the various threats faced by decentralized pools, block withholding attacks stand out due to their potential to increase revenue for attackers while simultaneously decreasing the competitiveness of the targeted pool.
A key consideration involves comparing the effectiveness of block withholding strategies versus Pool Sabotage Gain (PSG) attacks. In scenarios where no Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocol (DCPP) exists, PSG attacks become highly lucrative, granting immediate earnings to attackers and undermining overall pool stability. Nevertheless, even a modestly designed DCPP can significantly deter PSG attacks, making them far less attractive as a vector for exploitation.
The fundamental appeal of advanced DCPPs lies in their ability to reduce participation fees, which enhances the competitiveness of decentralized pools. Achieving the right protocol design, potentially including covenants, is essential to address attack vectors effectively without inadvertently incentivizing undesirable behaviors. Should protocol enshrinement prove impractical, attention must shift to refining the weighting and selection mechanisms within mining pools, all while remaining vigilant against introducing new vulnerabilities. The ongoing stewardship and active discourse within the community play a pivotal role in ensuring resilient and secure decentralized mining infrastructure.
